subject: Post-call recap & ops checklist: throughput knobs, tool-calling, and autoscale for SentryAI PoC
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Monroe <alex.monroe@sentryai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap & ops checklist: throughput knobs, tool-calling, and autoscale for SentryAI PoC

Thanks again for the call today — appreciate the clear signal around the two workload profiles you want to validate in the PoC (Burst QPS for Assist endpoints, and sustained throughput for nightly batch reranking). Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can line up Dedicated sizing and the SDK/auth pieces: 

Summary of asks from SentryAI:
- Assist endpoints: up to 600 concurrent short-chat requests during business hours with p95 latency target < 120ms
- Nightly reranker/embeddings job: 1.2M docs/day, batched; want to test embeddings + reranker latency/cost trade offs
- Structured output + tool calling: need demo of tool invocation pattern that returns JSON and triggers a downstream webhook

Immediate Redwood items (owners):
1) Autoscale sizing proposal and queuing strategy — Connor to propose queue partitions and concurrency caps that keep p95 < 120ms for Assist.
2) SDK + Auth quickstart — Marissa to provide code snippet for SDK setup (API key vs. mTLS for Private) and an auth matrix for Dedicated vs. Private.
3) Tool-calling demo plan — Ben to prepare a minimal workflow showing structured output + webhook firing and fallback model route.
4) Cost/throughput estimate — attached spreadsheet with a conservative reserve.

Attachments: redwood-poc-autoscale-playbook.pdf (playbook), capacity-estimate-q2-2027.xlsx (spreadsheet), sentry-poc-demo-scenarios.docx (your scenarios pasted into a doc)

Can we lock in the PoC start window the week of May 17? If that works, Connor will throw together an autoscale config and a short validation plan by May 7. Alex — any missing items on the asks above?

Thanks,
Ben
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0134

Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 18:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & ops checklist: throughput knobs, tool-calling, and autoscale for SentryAI PoC

Thanks Ben — that summary is spot on. A couple clarifications from our side:
- For the Assist profile, the 600 concurrent is a short burst ceiling; typical sustained concurrency is ~120-150. We want the p95 SLA at sustained load and graceful degradation in bursts.
- Nightly reranker: we run a batching pipeline that ingests embeddings and then does a rerank pass. The main risk is memory limits during the rerank (KV cache + large context for the reranker).
- For auth: we prefer mTLS for the PoC in our VPC, but API key is OK for an initial hosted test.

Confirmed: week of May 17 works for kickoff. Please mark the playbook with a 'validation plan' step that includes: latency histograms (p50/p95/p99), token-cost per interaction, and a failure-mode test (model fallback to small-llama variant).

Appreciate you pulling the demo for structured outputs — we'll want the webhook payload format ahead of time so our infra team can stub the receiver.

Alex
VP Product, SentryAI
alex.monroe@sentryai.com

Subject: Re: Post-call recap & ops checklist: throughput knobs, tool-calling, and autoscale for SentryAI PoC

Adding the SDK/auth snippet and a few technical questions so Connor can size queues correctly: 

1) SDK/Auth options (quick):
- Hosted test: Redwood JS SDK with API key header (x-redwood-api-key). Example snippet attached in Drive link.
- Dedicated (reserved): we recommend mTLS for in-VPC Dedicated; we'll provide a bootstrap script for cert install and a short sample using our client with socket keepalives.

2) Routing and model fallback logic we suggest:
- Primary route: high-QPS low-latency cluster (quantized 8-bit small-llama variant for Assist)
- Fallback: high-availability general-purpose model in another region or lower-cost pool when latency SLO at p95 is breached
- Sticky routing: session affinity for chat KV cache; otherwise stateless routing for reranks

3) Queue/concurrency draft questions for Sentry to confirm:
- Max inflight per worker process? (this affects token parallelism and memory)
- Preferred behavior on queue saturation: reject vs delayed backpressure vs shed to fallback model

Connor — can you take these and produce a 1-page queue/capacity sketch + recommended concurrency caps? I'll include the SDK snippet in the shared Drive and the mTLS bootstrap as a short bash script.

Marissa

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call recap & ops checklist: throughput knobs, tool-calling, and autoscale for SentryAI PoC

Attached is the one-pager sketch (see attachment stub) — quick notes inline: 

- Architecture sketch: two pool types for PoC: Assist-pool (low-latency, high-priority) and Batch-pool (throughput-optimized). Use separate queues per pool.
- Concurrency caps (initial):
  * Worker process: max 8 concurrent in-flight requests (keeps KV per-process memory reasonable)
  * Pool concurrency: Assist-pool target concurrency 600 (spread across 75 worker processes => ~8 each), reserve 25% headroom for bursts
  * Batch-pool concurrency: sized for 1.2M docs/day with batch sizes ~256, parallelism 24 => conservative start
- Autoscale policy: scale on p95 latency + CPU/GPU utilization signals; min replicas = 4 for Assist-pool, max = 40 for large bursts.
- Queuing behavior: prefer backpressure (429 with Retry-After) for hosted demo; for Dedicated VPC PoC we can configure soft queueing with shed-to-fallback model for degraded pathways.

Action items I will deliver by May 7:
- PDF one-pager: autoscale + queue sketch (redwood-poc-autoscale-playbook.pdf)
- Example autoscale config snippet (k8s/horizontal-proxy) and a small load plan to validate p95 targets
- A minimal structured-output demo (tool-calling) that posts to a stub webhook; will include example payload and fallback flow.

Alex — can you share the webhook endpoint stub or a test endpoint we can hit? If not available, I'll provide a local ngrok pattern and sample payloads for your infra team to mirror.

Connor O'Brien
Principal Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.com
